claim: Bone regeneration is mediated by skeletal stem/progenitor cells (SSPCs) that are mainly recruited from the periosteum after bone injury.
source: Bone regeneration is mediated by skeletal stem/progenitor cells (SSPCs) that are mainly recruited from the periosteum after bone injury.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about bone regeneration.

claim: The composition of the periosteum and the steps of SSPC activation and differentiation remain poorly understood.
source: The composition of the periosteum and the steps of SSPC activation and differentiation remain poorly understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: A single-nucleus atlas of the periosteum at steady state and of the fracture site during the early stages of bone repair was generated.
source: Here, we generated a single-nucleus atlas of the periosteum at steady state and of the fracture site during the early stages of bone repair (https://fracture-repair-atlas.cells.ucsc.edu).
evidence: The authors describe their experimental work generating the atlas.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs express stemness markers Pi16 and Ly6a/SCA1.
source: We identified periosteal SSPCs expressing stemness markers (Pi16 and Ly6a/SCA1)
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on transcriptomic data.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs respond to fracture by adopting an injury-induced fibrogenic cell (IIFC) fate prior to undergoing osteogenesis or chondrogenesis.
source: We identified periosteal SSPCs expressing stemness markers (Pi16 and Ly6a/SCA1) and responding to fracture by adopting an injury-induced fibrogenic cell (IIFC) fate, prior to undergoing osteogenesis or chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is a major finding from the study based on pseudotime trajectory analysis.

claim: Distinct gene cores are associated with IIFCs and their engagement into osteogenesis and chondrogenesis involving Notch, Wnt, and the circadian clock signaling.
source: We identified distinct gene cores associated with IIFCs and their engagement into osteogenesis and chondrogenesis involving Notch, Wnt, and the circadian clock signaling, respectively.
evidence: This finding is based on gene regulatory network analyses performed in the study.

claim: IIFCs are the main source of paracrine signals in the fracture environment.
source: Finally, we show that IIFCs are the main source of paracrine signals in the fracture environment
evidence: This is based on cell-cell interaction analyses using CellChat.

claim: IIFCs have a crucial paracrine role during fracture healing.
source: suggesting a crucial paracrine role of this transient IIFC population during fracture healing.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the paracrine signaling data.

claim: Bone regeneration occurs efficiently without scarring.
source: Bones can fracture but regenerate themselves efficiently without scarring.
evidence: This is established knowledge about bone regeneration.

claim: SSPCs are activated during the inflammatory phase of healing and differentiate into osteoblasts and/or chondrocytes.
source: SSPCs are activated during the inflammatory phase of healing and differentiate into osteoblasts and/or chondrocytes to repair bone via a combination of intramembranous and endochondral ossification.
evidence: This is established knowledge about bone healing processes.

claim: During intramembranous ossification, SSPCs differentiate directly into osteoblasts.
source: During intramembranous ossification, SSPCs differentiate directly into osteoblasts
evidence: This is established knowledge about bone formation.

claim: During endochondral ossification, SSPCs first differentiate into chondrocytes to form an intermediate cartilage template subsequently replaced by bone.
source: while during endochondral ossification SSPCs first differentiate into chondrocytes to form an intermediate cartilage template subsequently replaced by bone.
evidence: This is established knowledge about bone formation.

claim: The periosteum is an heterogeneous tissue located on the outer surface of bones.
source: The periosteum, an heterogeneous tissue located on the outer surface of bones, is a crucial source of SSPCs during bone healing (Duchamp de Lageneste et al., 2018; Jeffery et al., 2022; Debnath et al., 2018; Matthews et al., 2021; Ortinau et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The periosteum is a crucial source of SSPCs during bone healing.
source: The periosteum, an heterogeneous tissue located on the outer surface of bones, is a crucial source of SSPCs during bone healing (Duchamp de Lageneste et al., 2018; Jeffery et al., 2022; Debnath et al., 2018; Matthews et al., 2021; Ortinau et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs exhibit a high regenerative potential.
source: Periosteal SSPCs exhibit a high regenerative potential.
evidence: This is established knowledge about periosteal SSPCs.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs display both osteogenic and chondrogenic potentials after injury compared to bone marrow SSPCs that are mostly osteogenic and skeletal muscle SSPCs that are mostly chondrogenic.
source: They display both osteogenic and chondrogenic potentials after injury compared to bone marrow SSPCs that are mostly osteogenic and skeletal muscle SSPCs that are mostly chondrogenic (Duchamp de Lageneste et al., 2018; Jeffery et al., 2022; Julien et al., 2020; Julien et al., 2021; Matsushita et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs are still poorly characterized and their response to bone injury remains elusive.
source: Periosteal SSPCs (pSSPCs) are still poorly characterized and their response to bone injury remains elusive.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Recent advances in single-cell/-nucleus transcriptomic analyses provided new insights into stem cell population heterogeneity and regeneration processes in many organs.
source: Recent advances in single-cell/-nucleus transcriptomic analyses provided new insights into stem cell population heterogeneity and regeneration processes in many organs (De Micheli et al., 2020; Guerrero-Juarez et al., 2019; Storer et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Few studies have investigated bone fracture healing at the single-cell level.
source: However, few studies have investigated bone fracture healing at the single-cell level, and these studies have focused on cultured cells or late stages of bone repair (Julien et al., 2020; Sivaraj et al., 2022).
evidence: This identifies a gap in the literature supported by citations.

claim: A complete dataset of periosteum and bone regeneration is lacking.
source: Therefore, a complete dataset of periosteum and bone regeneration is lacking and is essential to decipher the mechanisms of pSSPC activation and regulation.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap that the study aims to address.

claim: Single-nucleus RNAseq datasets were generated from the uninjured periosteum and from the periosteum and hematoma/callus at days 3, 5, and 7 post-tibial fracture.
source: We generated single-nucleus RNAseq (snRNAseq) datasets from the uninjured periosteum and from the periosteum and hematoma/callus at days 3, 5, and 7 post-tibial fracture.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The analyses thoroughly describe the heterogeneity of the periosteum at steady state and the steps of pSSPC activation and differentiation after injury.
source: Our analyses thoroughly describe the heterogeneity of the periosteum at steady state and the steps of pSSPC activation and differentiation after injury.
evidence: This summarizes the findings of the study.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs represent a single population localized in the fibrous layer of the periosteum.
source: We show that pSSPCs represent a single population localized in the fibrous layer of the periosteum.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on spatial analysis.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs can provide osteoblasts and chondrocytes for bone repair by first generating a common injury-induced fibrogenic cell (IIFC) population that can then engage into osteogenesis and chondrogenesis.
source: Periosteal SSPCs can provide osteoblasts and chondrocytes for bone repair by first generating a common injury-induced fibrogenic cell (IIFC) population that can then engage into osteogenesis and chondrogenesis.
evidence: This is a major finding from the study based on trajectory analysis.

claim: The gene networks regulating pSSPC fate after injury were identified.
source: We identified the gene networks regulating pSSPC fate after injury
evidence: This is a finding from gene regulatory network analyses.

claim: IIFCs are the main population producing paracrine factors mediating the initiation of bone healing.
source: and IIFCs as the main population producing paracrine factors mediating the initiation of bone healing.
evidence: This is a finding from cell-cell interaction analyses.

claim: Single-nucleus transcriptomics provides results equivalent to single-cell transcriptomics, but with better cell type representation and reduced digestion-induced stress response.
source: Single-nucleus transcriptomics was previously shown to provide results equivalent to single-cell transcriptomics, but with better cell type representation and reduced digestion-induced stress response (Machado et al., 2021; Selewa et al., 2020; Ding et al., 2020; Wen et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: After filtering, 1189 nuclei were obtained from the uninjured periosteum dataset.
source: After filtering, we obtained 1189 nuclei, corresponding to eight cell populations
evidence: This is a data point from the study.

claim: Eight cell populations were identified in the uninjured periosteum: SSPCs, fibroblasts, osteogenic cells, Schwann cells, pericytes/smooth muscle cells, immune cells, adipocytes, and endothelial cells.
source: After filtering, we obtained 1189 nuclei, corresponding to eight cell populations: SSPCs (expressing Pi16), fibroblasts (expressing Pdgfra), osteogenic cells (expressing Runx2), Schwann cells (expressing Mpz), pericytes/smooth muscle cells (SMCs, expressing Tagln), immune cells (expressing Ptprc), adipocytes (expressing Lpl), and endothelial cells (ECs, expressing Pecam1) (Figure 1C and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on clustering analysis and shown in figures.

claim: Five distinct SSPC/fibroblast populations were identified expressing Pdgfra and Prrx1: Pi16+ Ly6a (SCA1) + cells, Csmd1+ cells, Hsd11b1+ cells, Cldn1+ cells, and Luzp2+ cells.
source: Subset analyses of clusters 0–5 identified five distinct SSPC/fibroblast populations expressing Pdgfra and Prrx1: Pi16+ Ly6a (SCA1) + cells (cluster 0), Csmd1+ cells (cluster 1), Hsd11b1+ cells (cluster 2), Cldn1+ cells (cluster 3), and Luzp2+ cells (cluster 4) (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from subset analysis shown in figures.

claim: Cluster 0 is the only cell cluster containing cells expressing Pi16 and stemness markers including Ly6a (SCA1), Dpp4, and Cd34.
source: Cluster 0 is the only cell cluster containing cells expressing Pi16 and stemness markers including Ly6a (SCA1), Dpp4, and Cd34 (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study shown in figures.

claim: CytoTrace scoring identified Pi16+ cells as the population in the most undifferentiated state.
source: CytoTrace scoring identified Pi16+ cells as the population in the most undifferentiated state (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from CytoTrace analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Prrx1 labels all SSPCs contributing to the callus formation including Pi16+ cells.
source: as Prrx1 labels all SSPCs contributing to the callus formation including Pi16+ cells (Figure 2D; Duchamp de Lageneste et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by data in the figure and a citation.

claim: Prrx1-GFP+ SCA1+ cells showed higher CFU potential compared to GFP+SCA1- cells.
source: Prrx1-GFP+ SCA1+ cells showed higher CFU potential compared to GFP+SCA1- cells, confirming their stem/progenitor property (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This is a finding from in vitro CFU assays shown in figures.

claim: Only GFP+SCA1+ cells formed cartilage after fracture indicating that GFP+SCA1+ cells encompass periosteal SSPCs with osteochondrogenic potential.
source: Only GFP+SCA1+ cells formed cartilage after fracture indicating that GFP+SCA1+ cells encompass periosteal SSPCs with osteochondrogenic potential (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a finding from cell grafting experiments shown in a figure.

claim: No marker was fully specific to one cell cluster and of the undifferentiated SSPC population.
source: We explored the expression of other known markers of periosteal SSPCs, including Ctsk, Acta2 (αSMA), Gli1, and Mx1, but no marker was fully specific to one cell cluster (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Duchamp de Lageneste et al., 2018; Jeffery et al., 2022; Debnath et al., 2018; Matthews et al., 2021; Ortinau et al., 2019; Tournaire et al., 2020; Gao et al., 2019; Chan et al., 2015; He et al., 2017; Böhm et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a finding from marker expression analysis supported by citations.

claim: A total of 6213 nuclei were obtained after filtering from the combined dataset.
source: We combined the datasets with the uninjured periosteum from Figure 1 and obtained a total of 6213 nuclei after filtering.
evidence: This is a data point from the study.

claim: The combined dataset was composed of 25 clusters corresponding to 11 cell populations: SSPCs, IIFCs, osteoblasts, chondrocytes, osteoclasts, immune cells, Schwann cells, endothelial cells, pericytes, SMCs, and adipocytes.
source: The combined dataset was composed of 25 clusters corresponding to 11 cell populations: SSPCs (expressing Pi16), IIFCs (expressing ECM-related genes including Postn), osteoblasts (expressing Ibsp), chondrocytes (expressing Col2a1), osteoclasts (expressing Ctsk), immune cells (expressing Ptprc), Schwann cells (expressing Mpz), endothelial cells (expressing Pecam1), pericytes (expressing Rgs5), SMCs (expressing Tagln), and adipocytes (expressing Lpl) (Figure 3B and C, Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the integrated dataset analysis shown in figures.

claim: After injury, the percentage of SSPCs was strongly decreased and the percentage of IIFCs progressively increased.
source: After injury, the percentage of SSPCs was strongly decreased and the percentage of IIFCs progressively increased (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from temporal analysis shown in figures.

claim: The percentage of chondrocytes and osteoblasts increased from day 3 post-fracture.
source: The percentage of chondrocytes and osteoblasts increased from day 3 post-fracture.
evidence: This is a finding from temporal analysis.

claim: Immune cells were drastically increased at day 3 after injury, before progressively decreasing at days 5 and 7 post-fracture.
source: Immune cells were drastically increased at day 3 after injury, before progressively decreasing at days 5 and 7 post-fracture (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from temporal analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Pi16-expressing SSPCs were located within the fibrous layer.
source: Pi16-expressing SSPCs were located within the fibrous layer, while Postn-expressing cells were found in the cambium layer and corresponded to Runx2-expressing osteogenic cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from spatial analysis shown in figures.

claim: Postn-expressing cells were found in the cambium layer and corresponded to Runx2-expressing osteogenic cells.
source: Pi16-expressing SSPCs were located within the fibrous layer, while Postn-expressing cells were found in the cambium layer and corresponded to Runx2-expressing osteogenic cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a finding from spatial analysis shown in figures.

claim: Postn expression was strongly increased in response to fracture, specifically in IIFCs.
source: Although Postn expression was weak in uninjured periosteum, Postn expression was strongly increased in response to fracture, specifically in IIFCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is a finding from expression analysis shown in figures.

claim: At day 3 post-fracture, periosteal thickening and the formation of a fibrous hematoma were observed.
source: At day 3 post-fracture, we observed periosteal thickening and the formation of a fibrous hematoma (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an observation from histological analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Pi16-expressing SSPCs were not detected at day 3 post-fracture.
source: We did not detect Pi16-expressing SPPCs, consistent with the absence of cells expressing SSPC markers in the day 3 snRNAseq dataset compared to uninjured periosteum (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from spatial and transcriptomic analysis shown in a figure.

claim: POSTN+ IIFCs and immune cells were the main populations present in hematoma and activated periosteum at day 3 post-fracture.
source: POSTN+ IIFCs and immune cells were the main populations present in hematoma and activated periosteum.
evidence: This is a finding from spatial analysis.

claim: At days 5 and 7 post-fracture, the callus was formed mainly of fibrotic tissue, new bone formed on the periosteal surface at the periphery of the callus and small cartilage islets were detected in the center of the callus near the periosteal surface.
source: At days 5 and 7 post-fracture, the callus was formed mainly of fibrotic tissue, new bone formed on the periosteal surface at the periphery of the callus and small cartilage islets were detected in the center of the callus near the periosteal surface (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This is an observation from histological analysis shown in figures.

claim: The fibrotic tissue contained mostly IIFCs, as well as immune and endothelial cells.
source: The fibrotic tissue contained mostly IIFCs, as well as immune and endothelial cells.
evidence: This is a finding from spatial analysis.

claim: SOX9+ and OSX+ cells were observed in the fibrotic tissue.
source: We also observed SOX9+ and OSX+ cells in the fibrotic tissue
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: The cartilage was solely composed of SOX9+ chondrocytes.
source: while the cartilage was solely composed of SOX9+ chondrocytes.
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: OSX+ osteoblasts were the main cell population detected in the new bone at the periosteal surface.
source: OSX+ osteoblasts were the main cell population detected in the new bone at the periosteal surface.
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence analysis.

claim: A progressive reduction of POSTN+ cells and immune cells from days 5 to 7 and increased vascularization in the newly formed bone were observed.
source: We also observed a progressive reduction of POSTN+ cells and immune cells from days 5 to 7 and increased vascularization in the newly formed bone (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This is a finding from temporal spatial analysis shown in figures.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs differentiate in three stages starting from the pSSPC population.
source: We identified that pSSPCs differentiate in three stages starting from the pSSPC population (expressing Ly6a, Pi16, and Cd34), predominant in the uninjured dataset (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from pseudotime trajectory analysis shown in figures.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs transition through an injury-induced fibrogenic stage predominant at days 3 and 5 post-injury.
source: Periosteal SSPCs then transition through an injury-induced fibrogenic stage predominant at days 3 and 5 post-injury.
evidence: This is a finding from pseudotime trajectory analysis.

claim: In the intermediate fibrogenic stage, IIFCs express high levels of extracellular matrix genes, such as Postn, Aspn, and collagens.
source: In this intermediate fibrogenic stage, IIFCs express high levels of extracellular matrix genes, such as Postn, Aspn, and collagens.
evidence: This is a finding from gene expression analysis.

claim: IIFCs differentiate into chondrocytes or osteoblasts, both predominant at days 5 and 7.
source: Subsequently, IIFCs differentiate into chondrocytes (expressing Acan, Col2a1, and Sox9) or osteoblasts (expressing Sp7, Alpl, and Ibsp), both predominant at days 5 and 7 (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is a finding from pseudotime trajectory analysis shown in figures.

claim: A parallel was observed between pseudotime and the time points of the dataset, confirming that the differentiation trajectory follows the timing of cell differentiation.
source: We observed a parallel between pseudotime and the time points of the dataset, confirming that the differentiation trajectory follows the timing of cell differentiation (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from pseudotime analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs respond to fracture via an injury-induced fibrogenic stage common to chondrogenesis and osteogenesis and independent of their final fate.
source: These results show that pSSPCs respond to fracture via an injury-induced fibrogenic stage common to chondrogenesis and osteogenesis and independent of their final fate (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the trajectory analysis shown in a figure.

claim: A progressive increase in SOX9 and OSX signals in IIFCs at the fibrosis-to-cartilage and fibrosis-to-bone transition zones was observed.
source: We observed a progressive increase in SOX9 and OSX signals in IIFCs at the fibrosis-to-cartilage and fibrosis-to-bone transition zones, respectively (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from immunofluorescence analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Grafted GFP+ pSSPCs formed POSTN+ IIFCs at day 5 post-fracture.
source: We observed that grafted GFP+ pSSPCs formed POSTN+ IIFCs at day 5 post-fracture (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from cell grafting experiments shown in a figure.

claim: Grafted GFP+ IIFCs formed bone and cartilage at day 14 post-fracture.
source: We grafted the GFP+ IIFCs at the fracture site of wild-type hosts and showed that grafted cells formed bone and cartilage at day 14 post-fracture.
evidence: This is a finding from cell grafting experiments.

claim: Periosteal SSPCs first become IIFCs that differentiate into osteoblasts and chondrocytes.
source: These results confirmed that pSSPCs first become IIFCs that differentiate into osteoblasts and chondrocytes.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the grafting experiments.

claim: Gene Ontology analyses of upregulated genes in IIFCs showed enrichment in GOs related to tissue development, extracellular matrix (ECM), and ossification.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analyses of upregulated genes in IIFCs (clusters 2–6) showed enrichment in GOs related to tissue development, extracellular matrix (ECM), and ossification (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a finding from GO analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Several ECM-related genes are specifically upregulated in IIFCs, including collagens (Col3a1, Col5a1, Col8a1, Col12a1), Postn, and Aspn.
source: We identified several ECM-related genes specifically upregulated in IIFCs, including collagens (Col3a1, Col5a1, Col8a1, Col12a1), Postn, and Aspn (Figure 7B and C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from gene expression analysis shown in figures.

claim: GO terms related to cell signaling, migration, differentiation, and proliferation were identified in IIFCs.
source: We also identified GO terms related to cell signaling, migration, differentiation, and proliferation, classic hallmarks of injury response.
evidence: This is a finding from GO analysis.

claim: Only a small subset of IIFCs undergo apoptosis.
source: Only a small subset of IIFCs undergo apoptosis, further supporting that IIFCs are maintained in the fracture environment giving rise to osteoblasts and chondrocytes (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from apoptosis analysis shown in a figure.

claim: 280 activated regulons were identified in the subset dataset.
source: We identified 280 activated regulons (transcription factor/TF and their target genes) in the subset dataset.
evidence: This is a finding from gene regulatory network analysis.

claim: SSPC, IIFC, chondrocyte, and osteoblast populations were identified through GRN-based tSNE clustering.
source: We performed GRN-based tSNE clustering and identified SSPC, IIFC, chondrocyte, and osteoblast populations (Figure 7D and E, Figure 7—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from GRN analysis shown in figures.

claim: Fibroblasts from uninjured periosteum clustered separately from the other populations, suggesting the absence of their contribution to bone healing.
source: Fibroblasts from uninjured periosteum (Hsd11b1+, Cldn1+, and Luzp2+ cells and corresponding to cluster 10 of Figure 5B) clustered separately from the other populations, suggesting the absence of their contribution to bone healing.
evidence: This is an inference from GRN clustering analysis.

claim: SSPCs are the most stable cell population with the highest number of activated regulons.
source: Analysis of the number of activated regulons per cell indicated that SSPCs are the most stable cell population (higher number of activated regulons), while IIFCs are the less stable population, confirming their transient state (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis shown in a figure.

claim: IIFCs are the less stable population, confirming their transient state.
source: Analysis of the number of activated regulons per cell indicated that SSPCs are the most stable cell population (higher number of activated regulons), while IIFCs are the less stable population, confirming their transient state (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis shown in a figure.

claim: SSPCs showed activated regulons linked to stemness, including Hoxa10, Klf4, Pitx1, and Mta3.
source: SSPCs showed activated regulons linked to stemness, including Hoxa10 (16g), Klf4 (346g), Pitx1 (10g), and Mta3 (228g) (Leclerc et al., 2023; Nemec et al., 2017; Takahashi and Yamanaka, 2006)
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis supported by citations.

claim: SSPCs showed activated regulons linked to immune response, including Stat6, Fiz1, and Stat5b.
source: and immune response, including Stat6 (30g), Fiz1 (72g), and Stat5b (18g) (Chen et al., 2011; Kollmann et al., 2021; Tsuruyama et al., 2010; Figure 7G).
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis supported by citations and shown in a figure.

claim: Osteoblasts and chondrocytes display cell-specific activated regulons including Sp7 and Sox9, respectively.
source: Osteoblasts and chondrocytes display cell-specific activated regulons including Sp7 (18g) and Sox9 (77g), respectively.
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis.

claim: 21 regulons named fibro-core were upregulated specifically in the IIFC population.
source: We identified 21 regulons that we named fibro-core and that were upregulated specifically in the IIFC population (Figure 7H and I, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis shown in figures.

claim: Several fibro-core regulons, such as Meis1, Pbx1, Six1, and Pbx3, are known to be involved in cell differentiation during tissue development and repair.
source: Several fibro-core regulons, such as Meis1 (1556g), Pbx1 (11g), Six1 (20g), and Pbx3 (188g), are known to be involved in cell differentiation during tissue development and repair (Le Grand et al., 2012; Linares et al., 2015; Rottkamp et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2023).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Reactome pathway analysis showed that the most significant terms linked to IIFC-specific TFs are related to Notch signaling.
source: Reactome pathway analysis showed that the most significant terms linked to IIFC-specific TFs are related to Notch signaling (Figure 7J, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Notch signaling is increased in the IIFC stage.
source: We confirmed that Notch signaling is increased in the IIFC stage (Figure 7J), suggesting its involvement in the fibrogenic phase of bone repair.
evidence: This is a finding from signaling analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Notch signaling is involved in the fibrogenic phase of bone repair.
source: We confirmed that Notch signaling is increased in the IIFC stage (Figure 7J), suggesting its involvement in the fibrogenic phase of bone repair.
evidence: This is an inference from the signaling analysis.

claim: Chondro-core 1 is composed of 9 regulons specific to the transition of IIFCs to chondrocytes, including Maf, Arntl, and Nfatc2.
source: Chondro-core 1 is composed of 9 regulons specific to the transition of IIFCs to chondrocytes, including Maf (17g), Arntl (1198g), and Nfatc2 (37g)
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis.

claim: Chondro-core 2 is composed of 14 regulons specific to differentiated chondrocytes.
source: and chondro-core 2, composed of 14 regulons specific to differentiated chondrocytes (Figure 8A, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis shown in figures.

claim: Chondro-core 1 regulons are known to be regulators of the circadian clock or of the T/B-cell receptor cellular response.
source: Chondro-core 1 regulons are known to be regulators of the circadian clock (Npas2, Arntl) or of the T/B-cell receptor cellular response (Bach2, Nfact2, Nfkb1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the identified regulons.

claim: TFs from the chondro-core 1 are interacting with each other and are at the center of the interactions between the chondro-core 2 TFs.
source: STRING network analysis showed that TFs from the chondro-core 1 are interacting with each other and are at the center of the interactions between the chondro-core 2 TFs, including Sox9, Trp53, and Mef2c (Figure 8B, Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from STRING network analysis shown in figures.

claim: Chondro-core 1 is only transiently activated when IIFCs are engaging in chondrogenesis and precedes the activation of chondro-core 2.
source: We observed that chondro-core 1 is only transiently activated when IIFCs are engaging in chondrogenesis and precedes the activation of chondro-core 2 (Figure 8C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from temporal regulon activity analysis shown in figures.

claim: Chondro-core 1 activity was high in early differentiated chondrocytes and progressively reduced as chondrocytes underwent differentiation.
source: Chondro-core 1 activity was high in early differentiated chondrocytes (low Acan expression) and progressively reduced as chondrocytes underwent differentiation, while chondro-core 2 activity was gradually increased as chondrocytes differentiate (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is a finding from temporal regulon activity analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Chondro-core 2 activity was gradually increased as chondrocytes differentiate.
source: Chondro-core 1 activity was high in early differentiated chondrocytes (low Acan expression) and progressively reduced as chondrocytes underwent differentiation, while chondro-core 2 activity was gradually increased as chondrocytes differentiate (Figure 8D).
evidence: This is a finding from temporal regulon activity analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Transient activation of the chondro-core 1 allows the transition of IIFCs in chondrocytes.
source: This suggests that transient activation of the chondro-core 1 allows the transition of IIFCs in chondrocytes.
evidence: This is an inference from the regulon activity analysis.

claim: Eight regulons forming the osteo-core are activated in IIFCs transitioning to osteoblasts, such as Tcf7, Bcl11b, and Tbx2.
source: We identified eight regulons forming the osteo-core and activated in IIFCs transitioning to osteoblasts, such as Tcf7 (23g), Bcl11b (14g), and Tbx2 (36g) (Figure 8E, Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from regulon analysis shown in figures.

claim: The genes with the strongest interaction with the osteo-core TFs are mostly related to Wnt signaling.
source: STRING network analysis showed that the genes with the strongest interaction with the osteo-core TFs are mostly related to Wnt signaling (Figure 8F).
evidence: This is a finding from STRING network analysis shown in a figure.

claim: Wnt signaling plays a role in the transition from early fibrogenic activation of pSSPCs to osteogenic differentiation during bone repair.
source: This reveals the role of Wnt signaling in this transition from early fibrogenic activation of pSSPCs to osteogenic differentiation during bone repair.
evidence: This is an inference from the network analysis.

claim: The osteo-core activity is gradually increased and maintained in osteogenic cells.
source: We calculated the osteo-core activity and observed that it is gradually increased and maintained in osteogenic cells, showing that the osteo-core is required for the transition and maturation of IIFC into osteoblasts (Figure 8G and H).
evidence: This is a finding from regulon activity analysis shown in figures.

claim: The osteo-core is required for the transition and maturation of IIFC into osteoblasts.
